newsitem.title: USA: Foreign crude sellers fail to sway U.S. buyers.
newsitem.headline: Foreign crude sellers fail to sway U.S. buyers.

text.p: A growing list of foreign crude sellers failed to sway buyers in the U.S. Gulf Coast region on Wednesday, reflecting continued uncertainty over the timing of Iraqi exports and perceptions of excess supply, traders said.
"You don't want to get stuck with expensive crude and then Iraq starts selling big-time," a Gulf Coast buyer said.
Another buyer added that supplies are generally seen as abundant. "There aren't a lot of takers. People are full-up. There's just took much supply out there," he said.
Indeed, several August cargoes were still unsold, traders said.
Among the August stragglers were several Nigerian cargoes such as Brass River as well as Argentine Canadon Seco.
A U.S. refiner was also heard to be re-selling 300,000 barrels of Zaire crude, asking September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing minus $1.00 a barrel for prompt delivery.
September pickings were also piling up. Several companies continued to gauge buying interest for North Sea Brent despite the narrow trans-Atlantic arbitrage.
The September spread between WTI and Brent was around $1.20-1.30 a barrel on Wednesday afternoon, even with Tuesday.

A European company was considering selling Brent arriving either September 5-15 or September 25-30, asking around 35 cents a barrel ex-ship under WTI, or around five to ten cents a barrel under the benchmark including lightering costs, traders said.
So far, no buyers have stepped up to the plate for Brent.
"We're looking for alternatives," a regular U.S. Brent buyer said.
Among the potential foreign alternatives to Brent is Colombian Cusiana crude, which fetched 57 cents a barrel under October WTI for early September loading in the last transaction on Monday.
Other September offerings included two cargoes of Argentine Santa Cruz for September 8-10 and September 15-20, with offer prices around WTI plus 25 cents a barrel.
Bids are due on Thursday for Colombian state oil company Ecopetrol's offers of Cano Limon, loading August 26-31, and South Blend, loading August 20-30, traders said.
Bids are also due on Thursday for a purchase tender for 960,000 barrels issued by Chile's state oil refiner Empresa Nacional del Petroleo (ENAP). The crude is due to arrive September 16-20.
